units.title: Second night of power cuts for Gilliver and Brackwater
units.author: courier
units.text: More than 1,400 homes in Gilliver, Brackwater and the coast road lost power overnight, Sound Power Co-op has confirmed. The supply failed shortly after 23:10 and was restored in stages, with the last properties reconnected at about 01:40. The co-op said no customers were without power for longer than three hours.

units.author: courier
units.text: In a statement, the co-op said the most likely cause was a build-up of salt deposits on insulators along the coastal feeder, which can allow current to track across the surface in damp conditions and trip protective breakers. Network manager Corin Abbot said crews would inspect the line in daylight and that washing of the worst-affected sections would begin this week.

units.author: courier
units.text: Residents on the coast road said the cuts came with little warning. One Gilliver householder said her lights dimmed twice before going out altogether and that she lost a freezer drawer of fish. A Brackwater publican said he served the last half hour by candlelight and that his regulars 'took it better than the jukebox does'.

units.author: courier
units.text: The co-op said it could not rule out further interruptions while inspections continue and has advised customers to keep a torch to hand and to avoid opening freezers during a cut. Customers who lose power for more than twelve hours may be entitled to a payment under the co-op's standards of service. The fault line is staffed through the night.

units.author: courier
units.text: Ammet District Council said its emergency planning team was in contact with the co-op and that care homes on the affected feeder had backup generators. A council spokesperson said there had been no reports of injury. The cuts follow last week's storm, which brought down lines in Tollinby, and the substation fault at Brackwater earlier this month.

units.title: Gilliver watches the lights on Kittering Holm
units.author: courier
units.text: By Nell Ashdown. From the harbour wall at Gilliver, the Holm is a dark line on the water by late afternoon. After nightfall, residents say, a small cluster of lights appears near its northern end and stays there. 'You can set your watch by it,' said one retired net-mender. 'It comes on before the pub fills and it's still there when I let the cat out at six.'

units.author: courier
units.text: The lights belong to the work camp set up for the clearance of the island, which is being carried out by Grieve Land Services for the island's owner, Ardent Vale Holdings. The contract, approved by the council under delegated powers, requires the removal of all trees on the Holm within thirty days. Grieve said the crew were 'well supplied, in regular contact and working to plan'.

units.author: courier
units.text: Not everyone in the village finds the lights reassuring. Several residents said they had begun checking on them before bed. 'It's a small crew a long way out, and it's cold,' said a woman who has lived on the front for forty years. 'You notice when there's somebody over there. Nobody's been over there at night in my lifetime.'

units.author: courier
units.text: Ardent Vale did not respond to questions this week about the purpose of the clearance or the number of people on the island. The company has previously described itself as a 'patient, responsible owner' with no plans to announce. The Courier has asked the council whether any further applications have been made for the Holm and was told none had been received.

units.title: Tower block stairwell lights repaired after weeks of complaints
units.author: weypost
units.text: Lights in the stairwell of Dellow Court, the 14-storey block off Canal Street, have been repaired after residents spent most of the month climbing between the sixth and eighth floors in the dark. Kerrow Estates, which manages the block, said a faulty timer relay on the riser had been replaced and that the circuit was being monitored.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The residents' association said the repair was welcome but overdue. Its secretary said older tenants had been unable to use the stairs safely when the lift was out of service, which happened on at least four occasions this month. 'A maintenance issue is still an issue,' she said. 'We've been asking since the start of the month.'

units.author: weypost
units.text: The stairwell has attracted attention online after residents described hearing footsteps on the darkened flights. Kerrow Estates said it had found 'no evidence of unauthorised access' and that sound travels unusually well in the concrete riser. An acoustics consultant who has commented on recordings posted by residents told the Post that a stairwell 'will carry a cough from the bins to the roof'.

units.author: weypost
units.text: One family on the upper floors is moving out this week. The association said the move had been planned for some time and asked that the family's privacy be respected. Kerrow Estates said it would carry out a review of lighting timers across its other blocks in the city before the end of the year.

units.title: Night ferries stay cut as review goes on
units.author: soundfm
units.text: Sound Lines says its reduced night timetable between Port Ammet, Lisle and Gilliver will continue at least until the end of the week while a crew welfare review is completed. The last two evening sailings in each direction remain suspended. Daytime crossings are unaffected.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: The operator has not said what prompted the review. A spokesperson told Sound FM it was 'a normal part of looking after the people who look after our passengers' and that it would be inappropriate to discuss individual staff. The union representing ferry crews said it was being consulted and was satisfied with the process so far.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: Commuters from Lisle say the cuts are leaving late-shift workers with no way home. One hospital cleaner said she now sleeps on a friend's sofa in Port Ammet two nights a week. Sound Lines said a taxi-boat arrangement was being looked at for medical staff but could not give a date.

units.title: Winter puts big clearances to the test
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: With the year's first hard frosts forecast across the Marrow Sound, contractors on fixed-term clearances face the familiar winter squeeze: shorter days, brittle chains and diesel that thickens below minus five. 'Every hour of daylight you lose in December is an hour you were counting on in the spring tender,' one Tollinby operator said.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: The largest job in the region remains Grieve Land Services' thirty-day total clearance of Kittering Holm, now past the halfway mark in calendar terms. Grieve has not published a progress figure. Industry observers note that the piece-rate structure, at $100 a tree with a day rate on top, rewards pace but leaves little slack for weather or breakdowns.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Island work adds its own costs. Fuel, food and spares travel by boat, timber is stacked on site rather than hauled, and crews live where they work. A former site lead who has run island jobs told the Journal the hardest part is not the felling but 'keeping a small crew steady when there's nowhere to go in the evening'.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Softwood roundwood prices at the Weyhaven yards were flat this week. Hardwood firewood continued to climb on the back of the cold forecast and the recent power cuts, with one merchant reporting a waiting list for seasoned ash. Chainsaw hire rates were unchanged.

units.title: Council says grit stocks are ready for cold spell
units.author: courier
units.text: Ammet District Council says its salt barns are full and gritters will run on priority routes from tomorrow evening as forecasters predict a spell of calm, cold weather with hard overnight frosts. Priority routes include the Port Ammet to Tollinby road, the Brackwater junction and the ferry approaches at Gilliver and Port Ammet.

units.author: courier
units.text: Residents are reminded that grit bins on side streets are for public footpaths and should not be emptied onto private drives. The council said it had received complaints last winter about bins in Rope Walk being cleared within a day of filling. Pavements near schools and surgeries will be treated by hand where staff allow.

units.author: courier
units.text: The council's highways team said the temporary traffic lights at the Brackwater junction would remain in place during the cold spell, despite calls to remove them until the roadworks resume. Contractors said the lights are battery-backed and should keep running if the mains supply fails.

units.title: Night recordists wind up woodland sessions
units.author: soundfm
units.text: A group of amateur sound recordists who have spent the past week leaving microphones out overnight in Brackwater Woods say their sessions end this week. The group, who met through an online audio forum, have been trying to record night-time knocking sounds that some walkers have reported since the autumn.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: The estate's gamekeeper told Sound FM he had no objection to people recording birdsong but did not want anyone walking the reservoir paths after dark. 'There's deep water and no lights,' he said. 'I've found two cars in the car park at midnight this week. I'd rather find nobody.'

units.author: soundfm
units.text: One of the organisers, a software tester from Brackwater, said the group had collected many hours of owls, foxes, wind and distant traffic, and 'a handful of things we'd like to understand better'. He declined to say what those were. 'We're putting the files up for anyone who wants to listen,' he said.

units.title: Live: power cut on the coast road
units.author: soundfm
units.text: 23:12. We're getting reports of a power cut along the coast road again tonight, from Gilliver harbour to the Brackwater turn. Sound Power's fault map shows the coastal feeder out. If you're affected, please don't ring the studio, ring the co-op's fault line. We'll keep this page updated.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 23:31. Sound Power says around 1,200 customers are without supply. Crews are on their way from the Brackwater depot. A listener in Gilliver texts to say the harbour lights are out but the boats' own lights are on, so the harbour 'looks like a car park at a festival'.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 23:58. The co-op says it has restored supply to part of Brackwater by switching to an alternative feed. Gilliver and the coast road are still off. Our overnight team are running on the studio's own power in Port Ammet, which is unaffected, so you can keep listening.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 00:34. A message from the care home on the coast road: their generator came on as planned and residents are fine. The manager says the night staff have made tea for everyone who woke up. Thank you to everyone who has messaged asking about elderly neighbours.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 01:12. Sound Power says linesmen have found the section that tripped and are testing it before reconnecting. They say this is the same stretch as last night. Asked about the cause, the co-op repeated that salt deposits on insulators remain the most likely explanation.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 01:41. Power is back across Gilliver and the coast road. Total time off for most customers was about two and a half hours. If you're still without supply, check your trip switch before you call. That's the end of tonight's updates. Wrap up warm; there's frost on the way.

units.title: Corrosion 'most likely' cause of cuts, says co-op, as crews work nights
units.author: courier
units.text: Sound Power Co-op has said salt-fog corrosion on its coastal feeder remains 'the most likely cause' of the night-time power cuts that have affected Gilliver and Brackwater on consecutive nights. The co-op said it had begun washing insulators between the Brackwater substation and the coast road and would replace any found to be cracked.

units.author: courier
units.text: Network manager Corin Abbot said salt carried inland by sea fog builds up on insulators over the autumn. When the surface becomes damp, especially with dew in the early hours, current can leak across it and cause a breaker to trip. 'It is a known problem on coastal lines,' he said. 'It tends to show itself at night because that is when the dew forms.'

units.author: courier
units.text: Linesmen have worked through the night on each of the cuts, the co-op said, and overtime has been approved for the rest of the month. A union representative said crews were 'stretched but coping', and asked the public to be patient. 'They're up poles in the cold at two in the morning,' he said. 'Shouting at the fault line doesn't help.'

units.author: courier
units.text: Some residents have questioned why the cuts have continued since the fog cleared. The co-op said deposits do not wash off on their own and that frost and dew can be enough to set off a fault once the insulators are dirty. It said it expected the washing programme to reduce interruptions within a week.

units.author: courier
units.text: The co-op has published a list of the sections being washed each day on its website. It asked people not to approach linesmen working on the network and to report any fallen or low-hanging cables by phone. A spokesperson said there was 'no evidence of interference with the line'.

units.title: Calm and cold: frost warnings across the Sound
units.author: soundfm
units.text: The Marrow Sound Met Office has issued a frost warning for tonight and the next three nights as high pressure settles over the region. Temperatures inland could fall to minus six, with minus two on the coast. Winds will be light and seas calm, a change from last week's storm.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: Forecasters say clear skies will make for bright, crisp days but very cold nights. Patches of freezing fog may form in valleys around Brackwater and Tollinby around dawn. Drivers are being warned about black ice on untreated roads, particularly on the hill down into Gilliver.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: Pet owners are being reminded to bring animals in overnight and to check outdoor water bowls. The council says it will open its warm space at the Port Ammet library during the day for anyone struggling to heat their home. Sound FM's overnight show will carry gritting updates every hour.

units.title: City opens extra night shelter beds as temperatures fall
units.author: weypost
units.text: Weyhaven City Council has opened forty extra night shelter beds as forecasters predict the coldest nights of the year so far. The beds, at the Quayside Mission and the old fire station on Mill Road, will be available from 19:00 each evening until the cold spell ends.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Outreach workers said demand had been higher than usual this autumn, and that some rough sleepers had told them they preferred well-lit doorways to the parks. 'People want light and people around them,' one volunteer said. 'That's always been true in winter. It's just more true this year.'

units.author: weypost
units.text: The council has also asked bus operators to keep depot waiting rooms open overnight during the cold snap. A spokesperson for the city's main bus depot said night cleaners would be on hand and that the heating would stay on. Members of the public can report someone sleeping out through the council's outreach line.

units.title: Lisle commuters petition over lost night sailings
units.author: courier
units.text: More than 300 people have signed a petition calling on Sound Lines to restore its late sailings from Port Ammet to Lisle, suspended for a crew welfare review. The petition says shift workers, students and hospital staff have been left 'stranded on the wrong side of the water' for most of a week.

units.author: courier
units.text: The petition's organiser, an office worker who crosses daily, said commuters understood that crew welfare mattered but wanted to know how long the cuts would last. 'If the crew need support, they should get it,' he said. 'But nobody will tell us what the review is about, and that makes people guess.'

units.author: courier
units.text: Sound Lines said it expected to complete the review within days and would 'come back stronger', with improved deck and slipway lighting already on order. It did not comment on reports that a deckhand had left the company. The harbourmaster at Gilliver declined to comment.

units.author: courier
units.text: Lisle's community council has asked for a temporary late water-taxi. A retired teacher who sits on it said the island had managed with fewer boats in the past but that 'people now have jobs that don't finish at five'. The matter is due to be raised at the district council's transport committee next month.

units.title: Holm contract enters final third as cold bites
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Grieve Land Services' clearance of Kittering Holm enters its final third this week with the first hard frosts of the season forecast. Operators on comparable sites say cold, still weather is good for felling, with predictable falls and firm ground, but hard on kit and fuel.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Diesel suppliers in the Sound have issued their usual reminder that summer-grade fuel can begin to wax at around minus five. Remote sites without heated storage are advised to dose tanks with anti-gel additive in advance. Two-stroke users are reminded that cold mix separates if left standing.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Grieve declined to give a progress figure for the Holm, saying only that the job was running 'to plan' and that it did not comment on live contracts. The owner, Ardent Vale Holdings, has not said what the cleared land will be used for. No further planning applications have been lodged.

units.title: Letters: on the island, the ferries and the dark
units.author: courier
units.text: Sir, I read with dismay the growing chatter about the workers on Kittering Holm. These are people doing a hard job in a cold place for a wage. They are not a curiosity. I would ask the Courier's readers in Gilliver to keep their binoculars for the birds. P. Lennard, Port Ammet.

units.author: courier
units.text: Sir, night after night the power goes and we are told it is salt. My late husband worked the lines for thirty years and he would have had something to say about that. I don't know what's causing it, but I'd like the co-op to stop sounding so sure. M. Callow, Brackwater.

units.author: courier
units.text: Sir, might I suggest that before we all panic about the ferries, the lights and the island, we remember that this happens most winters in some form. The dark comes early and people talk. In the spring we will have forgotten it all and be complaining about the car parks again. R. Dunmore, Lisle.

units.title: Kerrow Estates to check stairwell timers across its blocks
units.author: weypost
units.text: Kerrow Estates will inspect stairwell lighting timers in all eleven of its Weyhaven tower blocks after a faulty relay left part of Dellow Court in darkness for weeks. The company said the inspections were 'precautionary' and would be completed within a month.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Tenants' groups at two other blocks said they had reported similar faults over the past year. A councillor for the Canal ward said she had written to Kerrow asking for a timetable and for the company to publish its maintenance log. 'People shouldn't have to climb stairs in the dark to get home,' she said.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The electrician who replaced the Dellow Court relay said the old unit had corroded contacts, a common fault in damp risers, and that the new one should 'outlast the building'. Kerrow said it thanked residents for their patience. The residents' association said it would be holding the company to that.

units.title: Live: cuts hit Brackwater junction and Tollinby road
units.author: soundfm
units.text: 23:44. Sound Power's fault map is showing a cut on the inland feeder tonight, not the coast road. Parts of Brackwater and the outskirts of Tollinby are off. Several listeners say the temporary traffic lights at the Brackwater junction have gone dark. Please treat the junction as unmarked and take it slowly.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 00:12. The council's highways duty officer says the junction lights should have switched to battery and they're asking the contractor why they didn't. A van driver has called in to say he's sitting at the junction waiting for someone to come the other way so he can wave them through.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 00:40. It is minus four in Brackwater, according to a listener's car. The co-op says crews are patrolling the inland line. This is a different section to the last three nights, which it says it is still investigating. We've asked whether the corrosion explanation applies here as well.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 01:15. Sound Power says the inland feeder tripped and reclosed twice before locking out. A spokesperson said that is 'what the protection is designed to do' and that a full answer on the cause would come after daylight inspection. Brackwater depot has three crews out tonight.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 01:58. Supply restored to Tollinby. Brackwater village is coming back street by street. The contractor has sent someone to the junction with a generator for the temporary lights, and our van driver says he's finally going home. Thanks to everyone who sent in updates.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 02:30. All customers on the inland feeder are back on. That makes three nights running with a cut somewhere on the network. The co-op says it will publish a fuller statement in the morning. We'll be asking them about it on the breakfast programme.

units.title: Four nights of cuts: what we know so far
units.author: courier
units.text: Parts of the Sound Power network have now failed on three consecutive nights. Two of the cuts were on the coastal feeder serving Gilliver and the coast road. Last night's was on the inland line through Brackwater to Tollinby. All three began between 23:00 and midnight and all were fixed before 03:00.

units.author: courier
units.text: The co-op's explanation is salt contamination on insulators, made worse by dew and frost. It says this accounts for the coastal cuts, and that the inland line, while further from the sea, also crosses the exposed ground above the reservoir where fog collects. It has not yet said what caused last night's trip.

units.author: courier
units.text: Independent engineers the Courier spoke to said salt tracking is a well-understood cause of night faults on coastal networks and that three nights in a row is unusual but not unheard of. One said the fact that lines reclose and then trip again suggests a fault that comes and goes, which is consistent with moisture.

units.author: courier
units.text: Not everyone is convinced. Some linesmen have suggested online that the pattern does not look like contamination. The co-op said staff were entitled to their views but that its engineering assessment stood. It said patrols had found no damage to the line, no fallen branches and no sign of birds or animals on the conductors.

units.author: courier
units.text: What to do: keep a torch where you can find it in the dark. Leave one light switched on so you know when the power returns. Keep freezer doors shut; a full freezer stays frozen for about a day. Check on neighbours who rely on electric medical equipment, and register them with the co-op's priority list.

units.author: courier
units.text: Compensation: customers off supply for more than twelve hours in one go are entitled to a fixed payment. None of this week's cuts has lasted that long. Businesses that lost stock should keep receipts and contact the co-op's claims team. The co-op said it would review whether repeated short cuts should count.

units.title: The questions Gilliver is asking about the Holm
units.author: courier
units.text: By Nell Ashdown. Since the Courier reported on the camp lights on Kittering Holm, readers have written in with questions. Who is on the island? How long will they stay? What will the land be used for when the trees are gone? We have tried to answer what we can.

units.author: courier
units.text: Who is there? A small crew employed by Grieve Land Services, led by a site lead. Grieve would not give a number but said the size of the crew was 'normal for a job of this kind'. They live on site in a cabin and camper, supplied by boat from Gilliver. They are due to finish when the contract ends in under two weeks.

units.author: courier
units.text: What will the land be for? Nobody has said. Ardent Vale Holdings did not respond to repeated questions. A planning consultant who follows local applications said there was 'nothing unusual about an owner clearing first and applying later', adding that land with permission for development is worth more than land with trees on it. Others in Gilliver suspect something more private.

units.author: courier
units.text: Is anything wrong? There is no evidence that it is. Grieve says the crew are well and in contact with the company. The supply skipper, who crosses several times a week, told the Courier the camp was 'tidy and busy'. Residents who watch the lights say they have seen them every night since the job began.

units.author: courier
units.text: Why does it matter to Gilliver? Several older residents told the Courier the Holm has had nobody on it overnight in living memory, and that the village is used to it being dark. 'It's not that we mind,' one said. 'It's that we look across and there's a light where there's never been one, and you can't help thinking about who's under it.'

units.title: Gilliver chandlery sells out of lamp oil
units.author: soundfm
units.text: A chandlery in Gilliver says it has sold out of paraffin and lamp oil for the first time in years, as the week's night power cuts send people back to the hurricane lamps in the cupboard. The owner said he had ordered more and that it would arrive on next week's van, 'if the van can get down the hill'.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: Some older residents say they never stopped. In Gilliver, the custom of keeping a lamp lit in a front window overnight goes back well over a century, according to the local history society, which describes it as a courtesy to anyone out on the water. Several younger households told Sound FM they had started doing the same this week, 'just in case the power goes'.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: Fire officers are reminding anyone using oil lamps or candles to keep them away from curtains, never to leave them unattended near children or pets, and to make sure their smoke alarm works on battery. Battery lanterns are safer and, the chandlery owner admitted, 'less trouble, but nobody wants to hear that'.

units.title: Night staff wait in loading bays as power fails at depot
units.author: weypost
units.text: Night-shift staff at a distribution centre on the northern edge of Weyhaven spent forty minutes standing in its loading bays in the early hours after the site lost power and its backup lighting covered only part of the building. Managers said the evacuation of the picking aisles was a standard precaution.

units.author: weypost
units.text: One worker said staff were told to leave their scanners and walk to the nearest dock door. 'The yard floodlights went, then the aisles,' they said. 'The only light was from the lorries parked at the doors with their cabs on. Everyone just stood in it and waited.' Power returned shortly before 03:00.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The operator said it would review its emergency lighting, which passed inspection in the spring. Sound Power said the cut was part of a short interruption on a feeder serving the industrial estate and was not connected to the faults on the coast. It has not given a cause.

units.title: Insurers press contractors on remote crew welfare
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Liability insurers are asking land-clearing contractors for more detail on welfare arrangements for crews who live on remote sites, according to two brokers who work with firms in the region. Questions now include how often crews are contacted, how they are lit and heated overnight and what happens if supply boats are delayed.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: One broker said the questions were 'overdue rather than alarming' and followed a handful of claims elsewhere involving falls on unlit ground. Another said insurers were watching coverage of island jobs in the Sound but would not be drawn on any particular contract.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Contractors told the Journal that premiums for remote work had risen modestly this year. One Tollinby firm said it now refuses island jobs longer than three weeks. 'It's not the felling,' its owner said. 'It's what happens to a crew after twenty nights of nothing. You want them home before that.'

units.title: Lift out again at Dellow Court as cold snap hits
units.author: weypost
units.text: Residents of Dellow Court were left using the stairs again this week after the block's single lift broke down for the fifth time this month. Kerrow Estates said an engineer was attending. It said the stairwell lighting, repaired earlier in the week, was working normally.

units.author: weypost
units.text: A ground-floor shopkeeper said he had been carrying shopping up for older tenants since breakfast. 'Fourteen floors and minus three outside,' he said. 'People want the lift. The lights are fine now, I'll give them that. It's bright as an operating theatre in there.' The lift was back in service by late afternoon.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The residents' association has asked Kerrow Estates to replace the lift's control board, which it says has failed repeatedly since the summer. The company said the board was 'under review' and that a decision would be made in the new year.

units.title: Live: Port Ammet harbour front loses power
units.author: soundfm
units.text: 22:58. A first for this week: the cut tonight is in Port Ammet itself. The harbour front, the ferry terminal and the streets behind the market are off. Our studio is on the other side of town and still has power. Reports are coming in that some streets lost power for a few seconds before it went for good.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 23:09. Our reporter Jory is at the ferry terminal. He says the lights along the harbour front flickered for nearly a minute before the cut, dimming and coming back in waves from the terminal end towards the old customs house, then went out. A man walking his dog told him it was 'like someone running a hand along the switches'. The terminal's emergency lights are on.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 23:30. Sound Power confirms around 900 customers are off in Port Ammet. The co-op says the dimming many of you noticed beforehand is what happens when a breaker tries to reclose onto a fault, and is not dangerous in itself. Please don't use candles near curtains.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 23:55. The hospital on the hill is unaffected; it's on a separate supply with its own generators. The duty manager asks people not to come to A&E to charge their phones, which apparently a few have tried. The all-night garage on the bypass has power and says its coffee machine is 'available for emergencies'.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 00:38. A crew has found the fault, according to the co-op, on a cable joint near the ferry terminal. They are not giving a cause yet. Jory says the frost on the harbour wall is thick enough to write in, and that the only lights on the water are the fishing boats and, far out, the Carrow Point light.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 01:20. Power is coming back to the harbour front in sections. The market streets are on. The terminal is on. We've had dozens of messages tonight and most of them were people checking on each other, which is nice to see at one in the morning. Jory is going home to thaw out.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 01:44. All customers back on in Port Ammet. The co-op says it will publish a statement on all four nights' interruptions tomorrow, and that it has asked an outside engineering firm to review its findings. That's the end of our live coverage for tonight.
